Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were identified from a comprehensive search in PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science without time and language limitations.
As far as we know, the present study is the first meta-analysis to ascertain the superiority of NIPPV compared to HFNC on the primary outcome of treatment failure in children with bronchiolitis.

Trials were enrolled if they met the following inclusion criteria: (1) RCT; (2) HFNC treatment was applied and compared with the NIPPV method, and (3) reported at least one of the following outcomes: the rate of treatment failure (defined as the author of each trial), the rate of need for intubation, and the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) length of stay.
participants were randomly divided in two groups: CPAP/NPPV group and HFNC group.
We conducted a trial of 50 children with bronchiolitis who were randomized to treatment with CPAP or HFNC.

We conducted a randomized controlled pilot study in infants with critical bronchiolitis ( n  = 63) comparing high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC, n  = 35) to continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP, n  = 28).
We conducted a single-center, prospective, parallel group, open-label, and randomized pilot study at PICU of a tertiary care teaching hospital from September 2016 to February 2017.
Eligible patients were randomized using on-site computer-generated block randomization schedule to receive either nCPAP or HHHFNC.

A randomized controlled trial was performed in five pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) to compare 7 cmH<sub>2</sub>O nCPAP with 2 L/kg/min oxygen therapy administered with HFNC in infants up to 6 months old with moderate to severe AVB.

outcome: Treatment failure as defined by each trial.
population: Children younger than 24 months hospitalized with bronchiolitis in five two-arm parallel randomized trials.
timepoint: The acute treatment-failure assessment period reported by each trial.
